parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Phosphine, $:\text{PH}_{3}$, and carbon monoxide, $:\text{CO}$, are monodentate ligands found in some transition element complexes.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why transition elements form complexes.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The formulae of six complexes are given in Table 6.1.

The abbreviation $en$ is used for 1,2-diaminoethane.

The abbreviation $dien$ is used for the tridentate ligand $\text{H}_{2}\text{NCH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{NHCH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{NH}_{2}$.

The $dien$ ligand forms three bonds to the gold ion in $[\text{Au}(dien)(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{2}\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ and $\text{Au}(dien)\text{Cl}_{3}$.

These three bonds all lie in the same plane.

The CO ligand coordinates through the carbon atom in $[\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}]^{+}$.

parts.text: Complete Table 6.1 to state the geometry of the first three complexes. Each complex is either square planar, tetrahedral or octahedral.

parts.text: Use complexes $[\text{Au}(dien)(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{2}\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ and $\text{Au}(dien)\text{Cl}_{3}$ to write an equation showing ligand exchange.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
One of the complexes, $[\text{Rh}(en)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}]^{+}$ or $[\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}]^{+}$, can exist in three isomeric forms.

Identify this complex and the types of isomerism shown.

parts.label: (b)(vi)
parts.text:
Draw the three-dimensional structures of the two isomers of $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{2}(\text{NH}_{3})_{4}]^{2+}$ in the boxes and identify the type of isomerism shown.
